name: AnyPS5
tagline: A tool that converts PlayStation 5 game files into programs that run directly on your Windows or Linux computer - no emulation needed.
sentence: Point it at a PS5 game's executable files and it produces a native Windows or Linux program, the way Valve's Proton layer lets Steam games run on Linux - but for PlayStation 5 titles.

board.say: PS5 games only run on a PlayStation 5. If you want to play them on your computer, there is no official way, and traditional emulators are years from running modern 3D titles at playable speeds.
board.eg: A PS5-exclusive game you want to play on your PC - there is no port, no official plan, and emulators can barely load the main menu of most games.

board.say: You run AnyPS5's converter on a PS5 game's program files, or use the web converter at boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5 (files stay on your device).
board.eg: Upload a game's executable files to the web converter, pick Windows or Linux, and download the converted program.

board.say: A PS5 game's decrypted executable files - the program and system module files from the game, which must be obtained separately from your own console.
board.eg: A decrypted ELF executable, plus the sce_sys and sce_module folders from the game.

board.say: It rewrites the game's code into a format your computer can run directly, and provides replacement system libraries that stand in for Sony's services.
steps: The relinker converts the PS5 executable into a native program for your system (a Windows .exe or a Linux binary)
Replacement system libraries handle what Sony's software would - memory, file access, controller input, and audio
The shader recompiler translates the game's graphics instructions into a format your graphics card understands
Controller mapping supports PS5 controllers, Xbox controllers, and keyboard/mouse through a configuration file
board.eg: The PS5 uses the same type of processor as PCs (AMD x86-64), so the game's main code can run directly without translation - only the system libraries and graphics need to be converted.

board.say: A native PC program that runs a PS5 game directly on your computer, without pretending to be a PlayStation.

outputs.eg: A Windows .exe or Linux program built from the PS5 game, running directly on your hardware
PS5 DualSense controllers, Xbox controllers, and keyboard/mouse all work through a configuration file

before: PS5 exclusives stay on the PS5. If there is no official PC port, the only options are buying the console or waiting years for emulators to mature.
PS5 emulators can barely reach a game's main menu. One leading emulator has 12 of 55 tested games reaching gameplay, and most crash early.
after: A converter that rewrites PS5 executables into native PC programs - no emulation layer, so in theory far less overhead.
A web-based converter that runs in your browser and keeps all files on your device - no uploads, no servers, no installs required for conversion.
uses_note: AnyPS5 is 74 days old and still in early development. Only one game is confirmed fully playable. No named real-world adopters outside the developer.

steps: Visit the [web converter](https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5) to see the interface - it converts PS5 executables to Windows or Linux programs in your browser.
To build from source, clone the [repository](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) and follow the build guide (requires CMake, a C++20 compiler, and Vulkan headers).
Check the [community compatibility list](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) for which games have been tested - only Dreaming Sarah is confirmed fully playable today.

If that scan passes: visit the web converter at https://boykopovar.github.io/AnyPS5 to see the interface. Building from source requires CMake, a C++20 compiler, and Vulkan headers. 10 minutes max.

footprint.disk: No installer size published. Built from source with CMake. Windows builds require MinGW-w64 GCC 15.2.0 specifically.
footprint.memory: No data found. Uses Vulkan for graphics rendering.
footprint.runs_on: Windows and Linux. The PS5's AMD x86-64 processor means game code runs directly on PC processors. The web converter runs in any modern browser (desktop Chrome or Edge for large files).

best_for: You want to follow the PS5-to-PC porting effort and try early builds as they mature - this is a front-row seat to a new approach
You are a developer interested in binary translation, shader recompilation, or system library reimplementation
skip_if: You want to play PS5 games on PC today - only one simple 2D game is confirmed working, and no 3D titles are playable yet
You do not have legally obtained PS5 game files from your own console - the project ships no games, firmware, or extraction tools
You want a polished experience - there are no prebuilt installers, and the project is 74 days old

alternatives.name: Official PC ports
alternatives.line: Sony has been bringing PS5 exclusives to PC officially - Marvel's Spider-Man 2, God of War Ragnarok, and others are already on Steam.

alternatives.name: PS Remote Play
alternatives.line: Sony's official app streams PS5 games to your PC, phone, or tablet over your network. Requires a PS5 and a good connection.

watch: **Only one game is confirmed playable.** Dreaming Sarah, a small 2015 2D platformer, is the only title that runs start to finish. No 3D game is playable yet. 100% shader coverage is a milestone, but system library reimplementation is at about 85% and many functions are stubs.

**Requires game files from a modified console.** AnyPS5 ships no games, no firmware, and no extraction tools. Getting the files typically means dumping them from a jailbroken PS5, which may violate your console's terms of service or local laws.

**Extremely early - expect crashes.** The project is 74 days old and has shipped only v0.1. Its own demo shows a game reaching menus and early gameplay before crashing. The developer says releases will follow only after a full game launch.

**Progress percentages are misleading.** The shader and library coverage numbers track only the functions the project has catalogued so far, not every PS5 system function. The true denominator grows as more games are tested.
